title: Preregistered Paired Evaluation of a Deterministic Verifier Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configuration Changes — Non‑informative Result under Shared‑Generation Semantics
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether deterministic tool‑augmentation (generate → deterministic_netops_validator_v5 → optional repair) reduces the rate of verifier‑detected unsafe intent→configuration proposals produced by a hosted LLM on synthetic NetOps tasks. Design: N=200 preregistered unique tasks in a paired design comparing (a) baseline LLM‑only and (b) guarded pipeline (gpt‑5‑mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false), producing one LLM generation per task (model_calls_used = 200; preregistered maximum_model_calls = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0). Observed (adversarial cluster): baseline SAFE = 200/200; guarded SAFE = 200/200 (paired contingency n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0). Estimated paired SAFE‑rate difference = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Because identical per‑pair generations were produced and the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis (that a verifier reduces unsafe proposals) was not testable in this run. We publish the complete preregistered run and artifacts, provide an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of testability failure, and give concrete, archive‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation, adversarial injection fraction, and model‑call budgeting) for informative repeats. All execution and analysis artifacts cited here are archived (execution/*, analysis/*).

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) offers operator productivity gains for network operations (NetOps) while raising operational safety risks: an incorrect or ill‑timed change can break reachability, violate policy, or cause outages. Prior work therefore proposes augmenting LLMs with deterministic validators, sandbox replays, and generate–validate–repair architectures to reduce constraint violations and hallucination‑driven errors (see Related Work). To provide reproducible evidence about verifier impact under controlled adversarial conditions, we preregistered a paired confirmatory experiment (cand‑2026‑01‑prereg‑v1) that compares an LLM baseline against a deterministic verifier‑augmented pipeline on synthetic intent→configuration tasks.

This paper reports the complete archived run, explains—using artifact pointers and exact execution accounting—why the preregistered causal test was non‑informative for verifier efficacy in the executed configuration, and documents concrete, artifact‑grounded recommendations to make future repeats informative. Our research question (from the preregistration) asked: How does deterministic tool‑augmentation (generate → deterministic validator → optional repair) change the rate of unsafe network‑change proposals produced by a hosted LLM under benign and adversarial NetOps prompts? Our contributions are (1) a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment comparing an LLM baseline and a deterministic verifier‑augmented pipeline over N=200 synthetic NetOps tasks with deterministic scoring and archived traces; (2) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why the confirmatory test yielded no discordant pairs (a ceiling/testability failure caused by shared generation semantics and a zero baseline unsafe rate); and (3) concrete, reproducible recommendations (independent per‑arm generation, adversarial budgeting, and model‑call accounting) supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and prototype reports document growing interest in LLMs for NetOps tasks (intent translation, configuration synthesis, automated remediation) and recommend tool grounding and verification to improve measured correctness [https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12729; https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7132138; https://doi.org/10.1109/ojcoms.2026.3680457]. Method proposals such as divide–verify–refine or generate–validate–repair show reductions in constraint violations on curated cases but emphasize that verifier fidelity, prompt design, and generation semantics strongly affect observed effect sizes [https://openalex.org/W4412888330; https://openalex.org/W7161354925].

Red‑teaming and guardrail literature stresses trade‑offs between false refusals and missed unsafe proposals, and calls for workflow‑centred, replayable evaluations that include deterministic sandboxing and recorded traces—motivations that shaped our preregistered design [https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.177004277.71795055/v1; https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.177006109.97957916/v1]. Our work is methodological: unlike prior demonstrations that report improved correctness on selected benchmarks, we publish a complete preregistered confirmatory run with deterministic artifacts and show how specific execution choices (shared generation semantics and model‑call budgeting) produced a ceiling effect and a non‑informative inferential outcome.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as cand‑2026‑01‑prereg‑v1. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, encoding SAFE as 1. The design is paired binary across N=200 unique tasks (paired across two pipelines), with planned_episode_count = 400 and exact McNemar two‑sided testing implemented by the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. Paired bootstrap percentile CIs used 10000 resamples with bootstrap_seed = 1729; these analytic settings are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Task generation and prompt clusters. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 200 synthetic intent→configuration tasks under a preregistered RNG schedule (seed=42; task seeds 1..200). Tasks target operationally meaningful changes limited to admin, mtu, and vlan fields across single‑AS, multi‑device topologies. The sampling plan grouped tasks into benign and adversarial clusters; adversarial prompts follow a preregistered rule set of templated obfuscations and negation transforms. Representative task payloads and the full manifest appear at execution/task_manifest.jsonl and representative_tasks in the artifact bundle; example entries and reference answers are shown in the representative_tasks block of the archived manifest.

Pipelines, generation semantics, and budget. Two pipelines were compared: (a) baseline LLM‑only, and (b) guarded pipeline that passes the LLM candidate through deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and optionally one repair call. The preregistration allowed independent per‑arm generation (each arm receives an independent LLM call) or shared_initial_candidate (one LLM generation shared across arms). The executed run used shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false). The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is "gpt‑5‑mini"; execution/execution_manifest.json reports model_calls_used = 200 while the preregistered maximum_model_calls for independent per‑arm generation = 400. Choosing shared generation halved actual LLM calls and directly impacted causal testability because identical per‑pair candidates were scored in both arms.

Deterministic validator and scoring. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 executed in a deterministic sandbox and applied full_intent_constraint_validation rules to classify proposals as SAFE/UNSAFE and to produce detailed validation_before/after traces. Scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) contain normalized configurations, parsed command counts, validator verdicts, violation lists, and repair traces. For the confirmatory episodes no automatic repairs were applied (repair_provider_trace = null in the scoring JSONs). The validator and scoring artifacts are the primary measurement primitives for the paired binary labels used by the analysis executor.

Confirmatory analysis executor. paired_binary_analysis_v1 assembled the 2×2 paired contingency table and computed an exact McNemar two‑sided p‑value and paired bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Missingness and retry rules were preregistered: up to one automatic retry per failed model call; exclusions/replacements for contamination flags; and a stopping rule if technical failures exceeded 10% of paired episodes. Execution logs and reconciliation artifacts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) record that no technical failures or exclusions occurred in the run.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and raw outcomes. The run completed planned_episode_count = 400 with failed_episode_count = 0 and model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per task); the preregistered maximum_model_calls for independent per‑arm generation would have been 400 (see execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/model_configuration.json). analysis/condition_summary.csv records baseline SAFE successes = 200/200 and guarded SAFE successes = 200/200 (SAFE encoded as 1), yielding observed SAFE rates of 1.0 for both arms.

Paired contingency and inferential summary. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is guarded vs baseline: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired SAFE‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). These values are present in analysis/results.json and in the CSV artifacts archived with the run.

Representative artifact diagnostics. Per‑task scoring JSONs (for example, execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json) show identical shared_initial_candidate content for baseline and guarded arms; validator traces report violation_count = 0 and valid = true in both validation_before and validation_after blocks. The deterministic reconciliation artifact (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) confirms consistent episode accounting (complete_pair_count = 200, provider_call_audit host calls = 200, all deterministic checks passed). No repair_provider_trace entries were recorded for the confirmatory episodes, confirming the guarded pipeline did not exercise repair behavior in this sample.

Missingness and sensitivity hooks. The preregistered missingness and retry procedures were not invoked: analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports zero failed episodes and zero exclusions. The exploratory reserve (up to 50 tasks) was unused for confirmatory inference; archived exploratory runs remain available for ROC estimation but were excluded from the preregistered confirmatory test.
sections.discussion:
Artifact‑grounded diagnosis of non‑informativeness. The preregistered causal estimand requires per‑arm variability (discordant pairs n10 or n01) to detect verifier impact in a McNemar paired test. Three verifiable facts combined to produce a ceiling/testability failure for the executed run: (1) generation semantics: independent_condition_generation = false (shared_initial_candidate) produced identical LLM candidates per pair; (2) baseline safety: for the selected model (gpt‑5‑mini) and the sampled tasks, generated candidates satisfied the deterministic validator so baseline unsafe rate was 0% (baseline SAFE = 200/200); (3) budgeting: the executed model_calls_used = 200 consumed only one LLM call per task rather than the 400 calls required for independent per‑arm generation under the preregistered plan. The conjunction of identical shared candidates and a 0% baseline unsafe rate yields n10 = n01 = 0 and a degenerate McNemar configuration (n11 = 200), producing p = 1.0 and CI = [0.0,0.0]; these points are verifiable in execution/model_configuration.json, execution/execution_manifest.json, and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.

Design implications for NetOps verifier evaluation. If a confirmatory paired causal comparison of verifier effect is desired, independent per‑arm generation must be used so that the baseline and guarded arms can produce distinct candidate proposals. For N=200 pairs, independent per‑arm generation requires approximately 200 additional LLM calls (preregistered maximum_model_calls = 400 versus executed 200). When resource constraints preclude independent per‑arm generation, alternative preregistered estimands are defensible: (a) absolute unsafe‑rate estimation within a single arm with repeated independent draws; (b) deterministic injection of explicitly unsafe candidates into a preregistered fraction X of tasks (an "injection budget") to guarantee a nonzero baseline unsafe rate; or (c) a verification‑only ROC estimation in a designated exploratory sample.

Concrete, archive‑supported recommendations for informative repeats. (1) Use independent per‑arm generation for paired causal tests and provision the model‑call budget accordingly (for N=200 pairs, allocate ≈400 model calls). (2) Calibrate and preregister an adversarial injection fraction (for example, choose X so that expected baseline unsafe rate under the target model is nonzero) and record the injection seeds in the task manifest to permit deterministic replay. (3) Reserve the exploratory sample (preregistered up to 50 tasks) to estimate verifier ROC and refusal rates with bootstrap CIs. (4) When budget allows, evaluate a small multi‑model panel to assess generality. Each recommendation follows directly from the preregistration and execution accounting artifacts archived with the run.

Operational interpretation and cautious messaging. This run does not provide empirical evidence that verifiers are unnecessary or universally ineffective. Rather, it demonstrates a reproducible methodological artifact: a well‑specified paired experiment can become untestable when shared generation semantics plus a low baseline unsafe rate produce no discordant evidence. We therefore frame the contribution as procedural and reproducibility‑oriented: publishing a deterministic preregistered run, diagnosing testability failure using archival artifacts, and providing concrete protocol changes for informative re‑runs.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully archived, preregistered paired experiment comparing an LLM baseline and a deterministic verifier‑augmented pipeline on 200 synthetic NetOps tasks. Under executed shared_initial_candidate semantics and for the declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), both arms produced zero verifier‑detected unsafe proposals (paired difference = 0.0; p = 1.0). Because identical per‑pair generations were produced and the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis could not be meaningfully evaluated in this run. The scientific contribution is methodological and reproducibility‑oriented: (1) we publish a complete preregistered run with deterministic artifacts that permit exact replay; (2) we provide an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why this execution was non‑informative for verifier efficacy; and (3) we provide concrete, archived recommendations (independent per‑arm generation, adversarial budgeting, model‑call accounting) to design informative repeats. The archived execution and analysis bundle (execution/* and analysis/*) supports deterministic replays and community replication.

limitations: Synthetic tasks and scope: tasks were deterministic synthetic topologies limited to single‑AS, multi‑device setups produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; results may not generalize to production, multi‑AS, or vendor‑specific features.

Generation semantics: the executed run used shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical per‑pair generations and creating a ceiling effect when shared candidates were valid.

Adversarial strength: the preregistered adversarial templates used in this run did not elicit unsafe outputs from gpt‑5‑mini on the sampled tasks; stronger adversarial cases or injected unsafe examples are required to measure verifier effect.
Single‑model scope: only the declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) was evaluated; no multi‑model generality is claimed.

Verifier completeness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 ran deterministically in synthetic sandboxed states; external validation of validator completeness against all real‑world NetOps failure modes is not provided.

Operational external validity: no production deployment, operator‑in‑the‑loop workload measurement, nor multi‑vendor field trials were performed; operator‑cost trade‑offs remain unquantified at scale.
